edges.description: Disrupted desmosomes release plakoglobin to the nucleus where it competitively suppresses canonical Wnt signaling
Loss of desmosomal integrity causes secondary loss of connexin43 gap junction plaques and altered Nav1.5 sodium-channel distribution at the intercalated disc
Mechanical uncoupling leads to cardiomyocyte detachment and death
Suppressed Wnt signaling activates adipogenic transcription programs
Impaired electrical coupling and reduced sodium-channel conduction create slow conduction and re-entrant circuits
Electrical remodeling contributes to right-precordial repolarization abnormalities.
Slow conduction can produce delayed terminal ventricular activation on ECG.
The tissue-replacement mechanism is expressed as fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium.
Fibrofatty tissue creates substrate for re-entrant arrhythmias
Progressive fibrofatty replacement impairs right ventricular structure and function.
Ventricular arrhythmogenic substrate manifests as ventricular tachycardia.
The arrhythmogenic substrate can manifest as ventricular ectopy.
Ventricular ectopy or tachycardia can be perceived as palpitations.
Ventricular arrhythmia can transiently reduce cerebral perfusion and cause syncope.
Ventricular fibrillation or fast ventricular tachycardia is the cause of arrhythmic sudden death.
Right ventricular dysfunction is the structural cardiomyopathy phenotype.
Structural right ventricular disease manifests as chamber dilatation.
Advanced ventricular dysfunction can progress to heart failure.
Endurance athletics and high annual exercise duration accelerate arrhythmogenic expression and lower survival free from sustained VT/VF.
Vigorous endurance exercise increases structural Task Force Criteria penetrance and accelerates progression to stage C heart failure.

nodes.description: Antiarrhythmic agents (amiodarone, flecainide) may be used adjunctively for suppression of ventricular arrhythmias when beta-blockers are insufficient.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Alternatively, amiodarone and flecainide have been reported to be useful

nodes.description: Beta-blockers (sotalol, metoprolol) are first-line antiarrhythmic therapy to suppress ventricular arrhythmias and reduce adrenergic stimulation.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Since ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest occur frequently during or after physical exercise or may be triggered by catecholamines, non-class III antiadrenergic beta-blockers are recommended.

nodes.description: Endocardial and epicardial substrate-based catheter ablation is used as an adjunctive therapy in patients with drug-refractory, recurrent monomorphic ventricular tachycardia or frequent ICD shocks.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Catheter ablation is an alternative in patients who are refractory to drug treatment and have frequent VT episodes (with a predominantly single morphology)

nodes.description: End-stage disease may progress to biventricular heart failure requiring transplantation. PKP2 mutation carriers are less likely to develop heart failure than non-PKP2 ARVC patients.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in plakophilin-2 gene (PKP2) are associated with better survival in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Patients carrying a PKP2 mutation were younger at diagnosis (p = 0.003), more often had negative T waves in V1-V3 (p = 0.01), had higher left ventricular ejection fraction (p = 0.04), and were less likely to present symptoms of heart failure (p = 0.01)

nodes.description: Loss-of-function mutations in PKP2 destabilize the cardiac desmosome, the principal cell-cell adhesion structure at cardiomyocyte intercalated discs. Plakophilin-2 normally links desmosomal cadherins to the intermediate filament cytoskeleton. Loss of PKP2 causes failure of mechanical coupling between cardiomyocytes, particularly under conditions of hemodynamic stress.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the desmosomal protein plakophilin-2 are common in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: In 32 of 120 unrelated individuals with ARVC, we identified heterozygous mutations in PKP2, which encodes plakophilin-2, an essential armadillo-repeat protein of the cardiac desmosome.

nodes.description: Vigorous endurance athletics and high annual exercise volume markedly increase age-related penetrance, Task Force Criteria fulfillment, life-threatening ventricular tachyarrhythmias (VT/VF), and progression to stage C heart failure in PKP2 and other desmosomal mutation carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Exercise increases age-related penetrance and arrhythmic risk in arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia/cardiomyopathy-associated desmosomal mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: The final study population included 87 individuals (46 male) from 51 families with a single copy of a pathogenic ARVD/C-associated desmosomal mutation (76 PKP2, 7 DSG2, 3 DSP, 1 DSC2, Supplementary Table 1).

evidence.reference_title: Exercise increases age-related penetrance and arrhythmic risk in arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia/cardiomyopathy-associated desmosomal mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: Endurance exercise and frequent exercise increase the risk of VT/VF, HF, and ARVD/C in desmosomal mutation carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Of 87 pathogenic AC mutation carriers, 56 were endurance athletes. Endurance athletes were more likely to have symptoms at young age, fulfil the 2010 TFC, and had lower survival free from VT, ventricular fibrillation (VF), and heart failure.

nodes.description: Epsilon waves are delayed terminal ventricular activation signals used as a depolarization/conduction criterion in ARVC diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Epsilon wave (reproducible low-amplitude signals after the end of the QRS complex to onset of the T wave) in right precordial leads (V1, V2, V3)

nodes.description: Avoidance of competitive and high-intensity endurance sports is recommended for affected patients and pathogenic PKP2 variant carriers because endurance and frequent exercise accelerate penetrance, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and heart failure, whereas reducing exercise volume lowers VT/VF risk among high-volume exercisers.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Therefore, patients with AC, and in our opinion also all pathogenic mutation carriers, should be advised against practising competitive and endurance sports.

evidence.reference_title: Exercise increases age-related penetrance and arrhythmic risk in arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia/cardiomyopathy-associated desmosomal mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: Among individuals in the top quartile, a reduction in exercise decreased VT/VF risk (p = 0.04).

nodes.description: Progressive replacement of right ventricular myocardium with fibroadipocytic tissue is the pathological hallmark of PKP2-related ARVC. This results from cardiomyocyte apoptosis and loss due to mechanical uncoupling, combined with nuclear plakoglobin-mediated Wnt/beta-catenin suppression that drives adipogenic and fibrogenic remodeling. The right ventricle is preferentially affected due to its thinner wall and greater mechanical stress.

evidence.reference_title: Suppression of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling by nuclear plakoglobin recapitulates phenotype of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous DP-deficient mice exhibited excess adipocytes and fibrosis in the myocardium, increased myocyte apoptosis, cardiac dysfunction, and ventricular arrhythmias, thus recapitulating the phenotype of human ARVC.

nodes.description: Histological hallmark of ARVC showing replacement of right ventricular cardiomyocytes with fibroadipocytic tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the desmosomal protein plakophilin-2 are common in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is associated with fibrofatty replacement of cardiac myocytes, ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

nodes.description: Loss of PKP2 leads to secondary reduction and redistribution of connexin43 (Cx43) gap junctions and voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.5) within the cardiomyocyte intercalated disc functional triad. Reduced gap-junctional coupling and sodium-channel conduction slow ventricular activation, creating an early arrhythmogenic substrate that can precede overt structural disease.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal connexin43 in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy caused by plakophilin-2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Reduced connexin43 expression and localization to the intercalated disk occurs in heterozygous human PKP-2 mutations, potentially explaining the delayed conduction and propensity to develop arrhythmias seen in this disease.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: Desmosomal dysfunction due to a gene mutation may give rise to loss of mechanical cell-cell adhesion, and leads to down-regulation and/or altered distribution of other intercalated disk proteins, i.e. gap junction proteins (Connexin43) and sodium channels (Nav1.5) [ 43– 45 ].

nodes.description: Cardiac transplantation is indicated for end-stage biventricular failure refractory to medical therapy. Combined endpoint of death or heart transplant was less frequent in PKP2 carriers than non-PKP2 ARVC patients.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in plakophilin-2 gene (PKP2) are associated with better survival in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Combined endpoint of death or heart transplant was more frequent in subgroup without PKP2 mutation (p = 0.03).

nodes.description: ICD implantation is the primary intervention for prevention of sudden cardiac death in high-risk patients with ARVC, including those with sustained ventricular arrhythmias, syncope, or significant RV dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: diagnosis, genetic background, and risk management.
evidence.snippet: However, at present ICD implantation is the only proven lifesaving therapeutic modality for fast VT/VF.

evidence.snippet: In 32 of 120 unrelated individuals with ARVC, we identified heterozygous mutations in PKP2, which encodes plakophilin-2, an essential armadillo-repeat protein of the cardiac desmosome.

evidence.reference_title: Plakophilin-2 mutations are the major determinant of familial arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia/cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: In 24 of these 56 ARVC patients (43%), 14 different (11 novel) PKP2 mutations were identified.

evidence.reference_title: The genetic architecture of Plakophilin 2 cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: We identify the PKP2 C-terminus as a potential functional domain and find that truncating variants likely cause disease irrespective of transcript position.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in plakophilin-2 gene (PKP2) are associated with better survival in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Ten variants (5 frameshift, 2 nonsense, 2 splicing, and 1 missense) in PKP2 were found in 28 (50%) cases.

evidence.snippet: Patients with AC typically present between the second and the fourth decade of life with palpitations, lightheadedness, or syncope due to ventricular ectopy or (monomorphic) ventricular tachycardia (VT) with left bundle branch block (LBBB) morphology

nodes.description: Frequent ventricular ectopy (>500 premature ventricular complexes per 24 hours on Holter monitoring) is a minor Task Force diagnostic criterion and contributes to palpitations and arrhythmia burden.

nodes.description: Progressive fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular wall leads to right ventricular dilatation, wall motion abnormalities, and eventual right heart failure. Some patients also develop left ventricular involvement, though PKP2 mutation carriers are less likely to develop left ventricular damage than non-PKP2 ARVC.

evidence.snippet: Two patients presented with syncope, and two with the sudden death of a young adult sibling, which were found at autopsy to have ARVC.

nodes.description: Ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation arise from the combined effects of gap junction remodeling (electrical uncoupling) and fibrofatty replacement creating re-entrant circuits. Arrhythmias may occur in the concealed phase before overt structural disease, driven by electrical remodeling alone.

evidence.snippet: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is associated with fibrofatty replacement of cardiac myocytes, ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

nodes.description: Desmosomal disruption in cardiac muscle cells causes nuclear translocation of plakoglobin, which competitively inhibits beta-catenin-mediated canonical Wnt signaling through Tcf/Lef1 transcription factors. Suppression of Wnt signaling in cardiomyocytes upregulates adipogenic and fibrogenic gene expression programs and intracellular lipid accumulation, driving fibrofatty myocardial remodeling.

evidence.reference_title: Suppression of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling by nuclear plakoglobin recapitulates phenotype of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: suppression of DP expression leads to nuclear localization of the desmosomal protein plakoglobin and a 2-fold reduction in canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through Tcf/Lef1 transcription factors. The ensuing phenotype is increased expression of adipogenic and fibrogenic genes and accumulation of fat droplets.
